{{Top}}
[[File:Airspeeders_negvv.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Airspeeder classifications]]
'''Airspeeders''', also known as '''aircars''' or '''flitters''', were [[Repulsorlift/Legends|repulsorlift]] vehicles common throughout [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]]. They were distinguished from [[Landspeeder/Legends|landspeeders]] by a higher operating altitude and normally higher top speed. Some were also equipped with boosters that enabled them to achieve low planetary orbit for a short time. They were not designed for orbital flight, though they could attain such high altitude that they pushed the boundaries of [[Atmosphere/Legends|atmosphere]] and space.

==Description==
[[File:Rebel_Snowspeeder.jpg|thumb|left|200px|A Rebel T-47 snowspeeder]]
Airspeeders were used for a wide variety of roles galaxy-wide. These included transportation, recreation, and offensive and defensive combat. The skies of many industrialized and/or urbanized planets, particularly [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]] and other [[Core Worlds/Legends|Core Worlds]], were often clogged with airspeeders. This became such a problem for [[Ecumenopolis/Legends|ecumenopolis]] such as Coruscant and [[Taris/Legends|Taris]] that they were forced to adopt a series of rigidly controlled [[Skylane/Legends|skylanes]] to which most civilian airspeeders were regulated. To fly beyond these lanes often required special dispensation from the government; this often required the pilot to demonstrate a degree of skill in handling his craft.

Standard government-model airspeeders were equipped with a [[speed governor]], an [[altitude limiter]], and a [[Pilot droid/Legends|pilot droid]].<ref name="BTS">''[[Before the Storm]]''</ref>

Many notable companies produced airspeeders, including [[Incom Corporation/Legends|Incom Corporation]], [[Tagge Company/Legends|Tagge Company]], and [[SoroSuub Corporation/Legends|SoroSuub Corporation]]. Even the [[Yuuzhan Vong]] produced a type of combat airspeeder analog called the [[Tsik vai]].

===Famous airspeeder types===
*The Incom Corporation [[T-16 skyhopper/Legends|T-16 skyhopper]] was considered the upper limit for airspeeder design when first produced. It was equipped with an [[Ion engine/Legends|ion drive]], allowing it much broader operating parameters, including low planetary orbits. Its controls were similar to other Incom designs, allowing civilian pilots like [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]] to quickly adapt to the [[T-65 X-wing starfighter/Legends|T-65 X-wing starfighter]].

*Another Incom design, the [[T-47 airspeeder/Legends|T-47 airspeeder]], was one of the most popular civilian airspeeders. It was modified by the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Alliance to Restore the Republic]] with weapons and tow cables for pulling cargo [[Skiff/Legends|skiffs]]. Later, when the Alliance established [[Echo Base/Legends|Echo Base]] on [[Hoth/Legends|Hoth]], they were further modified to operate in sub-zero temperatures. These airspeeders became known as [[Snowspeeder/Legends|snowspeeders]].
*The Alliance frequently turned [[Starfighter/Legends|starfighters]] no longer suitable for space combat into customized combat airspeeders.
*The [[Storm IV Twin-Pod cloud car/Legends|Storm IV Twin-Pod cloud car]] was another airspeeder with an additional ion engine for use in upper-atmosphere flight.
*The [[V-wing airspeeder]] manufactured by [[Slayn & Korpil/Legends|Slayn & Korpil]] for the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]] was one of the fastest combat airspeeder types ever produced.

==Behind the scenes==
[[File:BobaFettAirspeederModel-AotCTVD.jpg|thumb|200px|A model airspeeder]]
Author [[Aaron Allston]], in three of the four novels he wrote for the X-wing series (''[[X-Wing: Wraith Squadron]]'', ''[[X-Wing: Iron Fist]]'', ''[[X-Wing: Solo Command]]'' and ''[[X-Wing: Mercy Kill]]''), used the word "[[Skimmer/Legends|skimmer]]" as a catch-all term for both landspeeders and airspeeders, despite the fact that skimmers were a distinct class or subclass of repulsorlift vehicle.
